examples.ko: 따뜻한 말 한마디가 그의 분노를 누그러트렸어요.
examples.en: One warm word softened his anger.

examples.ko: 차를 한 잔 마시면 긴장을 누그러트릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Having a cup of tea can ease your tension.
Try easing the mood by speaking with a smile.

examples.ko: 그는 화를 누그러트리고 차분하게 이야기를 시작했어요.
examples.en: He calmed his anger and began to talk quietly.
I bought a gift to soothe my friend's anger.

examples.ko: 그 말이 팀장님의 화를 누그러트리지는 못했어요.
examples.en: Those words couldn't soften the team leader's anger.

explain: '누그러뜨리다'라고도 해요. '누그러들다'는 스스로 약해지고, 이 말은 사람이 일부러 약하게 만들 때 써요. 화, 긴장, 분위기처럼 마음에 관한 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It can also be said '누그러뜨리다'. '누그러들다' weakens by itself, while this one is used when a person deliberately makes something weaker. It goes well with words about feelings, such as anger, tension and mood.

examples.en: That critic is famous for his sharp tongue.
Many people have been hurt by his cutting remarks.

examples.ko: 친구가 농담처럼 독설을 던져서 조금 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My friend threw out a biting remark like a joke, and I was a little shocked.
Pouring out harsh words won't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 선생님은 독설 대신 따뜻한 조언을 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Instead of harsh words, the teacher gave me warm advice.
He's a host with a sharp-tongued image on TV.

explain: 상대 앞에서 날카롭고 매섭게 비꼬거나 비판하는 말이에요. 뒤에서 흉보는 '험담'과 달리 앞에서 직접 던지는 말이고, 상대를 위한 '쓴소리'와도 달라요. '독설을 퍼붓다', '독설을 날리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These are sharp, stinging words of sarcasm or criticism said right to someone's face. Unlike '험담', which is gossip behind someone's back, it is said directly, and it also differs from '쓴소리', which is tough advice for the person's good. Typical uses are '독설을 퍼붓다' and '독설을 날리다'.

examples.ko: 저는 말꼬리를 길게 늘이는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of drawing out the end of my sentences.

examples.ko: 친구가 자꾸 제 말꼬리를 잡아서 짜증이 나요.
examples.en: My friend keeps picking on my words, and it annoys me.
If the end of a sentence goes up, it sounds like a question.

examples.ko: 말꼬리만 잡지 말고 제 이야기를 끝까지 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just nitpick my words; please hear me out.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말꼬리에 힘이 없어서 걱정돼요.
examples.en: The end of his sentences sounds weak, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 회의 때마다 남의 말꼬리를 잡는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone who nitpicks other people's words at every meeting.

explain: '말끝'처럼 말의 맨 끝부분을 가리켜요. 말투를 이야기할 때는 '말꼬리가 올라가다/내려가다'처럼 쓰고, '말꼬리를 잡다'는 상대 말의 작은 흠을 트집 잡는다는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.example: 말꼬리를 잡고 늘어지면 대화가 끝나지 않아요.
phrases.en: If you keep picking on every little word, the conversation never ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 한 말의 핵심이 아니라 작은 표현이나 실수를 붙잡고 따질 때 써요. 대체로 못마땅한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone fixes on a small word or slip instead of the main point and argues about it. It usually sounds disapproving.

explain_en: Like '말끝', it points to the very end of what someone says. For speech style you say '말꼬리가 올라가다/내려가다', and '말꼬리를 잡다' means to seize on a small flaw in someone's words.

examples.en: Don't butt in on other people's business.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 말참견을 해서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Someone keeps chiming in next to me, so I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말참견이 심해서 같이 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: He interrupts too much, so it's hard to work with him.

examples.ko: 말참견이라고 생각하지 말고 제 얘기를 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't think of it as meddling and just hear me out.
The mood got bad because of pointless interjections.
The child got scolded for butting into the adults' conversation.

explain: 그냥 '참견'은 남의 일 전반에 끼어드는 것이고, 말참견은 남이 하는 이야기에 말로 끼어드는 것을 가리켜요. 대답이나 반박을 뜻하는 '말대꾸'와는 달라요. 보통 못마땅한 느낌으로 써요.
explain_en: '참견' is meddling in someone's affairs in general, while '말참견' is jumping into other people's conversation with your words. It is different from '말대꾸', which means talking back. It usually carries a disapproving tone.

examples.ko: 회의에서 그의 의견에 반론하는 사람이 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody argued against his opinion at the meeting.

examples.ko: 저는 그 주장에 이렇게 반론하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to rebut that claim like this.
To rebut an article, you need evidence.

examples.ko: 그는 비판에 바로 반론하지 않고 기다렸어요.
examples.en: He didn't rebut the criticism right away but waited.

examples.ko: 선생님 말씀에 반론하는 건 조금 부담스러웠어요.
examples.en: It felt a bit awkward to argue against what the teacher said.

examples.ko: 토론에서 상대 팀이 우리 의견에 반론하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: In the debate, the other team began to counter our opinion.

explain: '반대하다'는 싫다고 하는 거고, '반론하다'는 이유를 대면서 상대 주장에 맞서는 거예요. 토론이나 기사처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. 보통 '~에 반론하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: 반대하다 just says you are against something, while 반론하다 means you answer the other side's claim with reasons. It fits formal settings like debates and articles. The usual pattern is ~에 반론하다.

examples.ko: 그는 뱃심이 좋아서 사장님 앞에서도 할 말을 다 했어요.
examples.en: He has such nerve that he said everything he wanted even in front of the boss.
He's a newcomer, but what nerve he has.
I pushed ahead boldly, and the negotiation went well.

examples.ko: 뱃심 좋은 친구가 먼저 손을 들고 질문했어요.
examples.en: A gutsy friend raised his hand first and asked a question.
He is someone who sticks it out with sheer guts, whatever it is.
I lacked nerve and backed down at the crucial moment.

explain: 겁내지 않고 끝까지 밀고 나가는 힘이에요. '뱃심이 좋다, 뱃심이 두둑하다, 뱃심이 있다'로 쓰고, 비슷한 말 '배짱'과 자주 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 상황에 따라 '뻔뻔할 만큼 대담하다'는 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the strength to push on to the end without being afraid. It is used as '뱃심이 좋다', '뱃심이 두둑하다' or '뱃심이 있다', and can often be swapped with the similar word '배짱'. Depending on context it can also carry a sense of being almost shamelessly bold.

examples.en: The teacher explained it in fine detail.
The plan is detailed, so it's easy to follow.
Please check even the small details.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 모든 걸 세세히 기억해요.
examples.en: That person remembers everything in detail.

examples.ko: 안내서가 너무 세세해서 오히려 읽기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The guide is so detailed that it's hard to read.
I was grateful for my mother's careful attention to detail.

explain: '세세하다'는 작은 부분까지 꼼꼼하고 자세하다는 뜻이에요. '자세하다'와 비슷하지만 세세하다는 작은 항목을 하나하나 짚는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '세세하게', '세세히'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 세세하다 means attending to small points one by one. It is close to 자세하다, but with a stronger feeling of going through each little item. You mostly hear it as 세세하게 or 세세히.

examples.en: I know it is a bother, but please check just once.
Preparing to move is more of a hassle than you think.
Guiding each guest one by one was laborious.
If it is too much trouble, I will do it for you.

examples.ko: 수고롭지 않다면 문 좀 열어 주실래요?
examples.en: If it is no trouble, could you open the door?
Getting up at dawn every day is a burden.

explain: '수고롭다'는 일이 번거롭고 애써야 해서 힘들 때 써요. 부탁할 때 '수고로우시겠지만'을 앞에 붙이면 정중해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '수고로워요', '수고로운'이 돼요. 일을 마친 사람에게 하는 인사 '수고했어요'와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: '수고롭다' describes something that takes bothersome effort. Putting '수고로우시겠지만' before a request makes it polite. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, giving '수고로워요' and '수고로운'. It is used differently from the greeting '수고했어요' said to someone who finished work.

examples.ko: 거절할 때는 완곡히 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When you turn something down, it's better to say it indirectly.
The teacher politely turned down my request.

examples.ko: 상대방이 기분 나쁘지 않게 완곡히 표현해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to put it gently so the other person doesn't feel bad.
The department head hinted, in a roundabout way, that I should quit.
I politely declined that offer.
Even though I put it gently, my friend felt hurt.

explain: 하기 어려운 말을 부드럽게 돌려서 할 때 써요. '거절하다, 말하다, 표현하다'와 자주 같이 나오고, 반대로 말하면 '직접', '딱 잘라'예요. 말할 때는 '완곡하게'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Use it when you say something hard in a soft, roundabout way. It often goes with 거절하다, 말하다 and 표현하다, and the opposite idea is '직접' or '딱 잘라'. In speech, '완곡하게' often sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 부장님이 그 일까지 결정하는 건 월권이에요.
examples.en: It's overstepping for the department head to decide even that.
It's not my job, so would it be overstepping to say something?
I'm being careful because I might be told I'm overstepping.

examples.ko: 월권 아니냐는 지적이 직원들 사이에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: Some employees pointed out that it might be overstepping.
That's close to overstepping for an intern to do.

examples.ko: 팀장이 제 업무에 간섭하는 건 월권이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think it's overstepping for the team leader to interfere in my work.

explain: '월권이다', '월권을 하다'처럼 말하고, 맡은 권한의 범위를 넘어 남의 몫에 끼어들었을 때 써요. '주제넘다'는 태도 전반을 말하지만 '월권'은 권한의 범위에 초점이 있어요. '월권인 줄 알지만'처럼 조심스럽게 말을 꺼낼 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '월권이다' or '월권을 하다' when someone goes beyond their assigned authority and steps into someone else's area. '주제넘다' is about attitude in general, while '월권' focuses on the limits of authority. It is also used to open a careful remark, as in '월권인 줄 알지만'.

examples.en: The scenery I saw on the trip was truly rare and wonderful.
The market was full of exotic fruit.
Every exhibit in this museum is rare and curious.

examples.ko: 그 마을의 풍경이 너무 진기해서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: The village scenery was so unusual that I took lots of photos.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 젊을 때 본 진기한 일을 들려주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather told me about a remarkable thing he saw when he was young.
I picked up a stone with an unusual shape.

explain: 드물고 귀해서 구경할 만한 물건, 풍경, 일에 써요. '신기하다'와 비슷하지만 '진기하다'는 대상 자체가 보기 드물다는 느낌이 있어요. 말할 때는 '신기하다'로 바꿔도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes objects, scenery or events that are rare and worth seeing. It is close to '신기하다', but '진기하다' stresses that the thing itself is uncommon. In speech you can swap in '신기하다' and it still sounds natural.

examples.en: I think privacy is important.
Please respect other people's privacy.
If a room has no door, there is no privacy.
That article invaded the celebrity's privacy.

examples.ko: 프라이버시 때문에 사진은 올릴 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't post photos because of privacy.
Please check your privacy settings.

explain: '프라이버시'는 남이 모르게 하고 싶은 개인 생활이에요. 보통 '프라이버시를 지키다', '프라이버시를 침해하다'처럼 말해요. 한국어로 '사생활'이라고도 하는데, 일상에서는 '사생활'이 더 자연스러운 때가 많아요.
explain_en: 프라이버시 is the part of personal life that you want to keep away from others. People say 프라이버시를 지키다 or 프라이버시를 침해하다. The Korean word 사생활 means the same thing, and in daily speech it often sounds more natural.
